## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized carpenter ant characterized by its compact body, dark head and abdomen, reddish to brownish thorax, and quick movements along vegetation and structures. In Florida, it is common in trees, shrubs, palms, gardens, hammocks, parks, yards, and urban areas where cavities, dead twigs, or hollow plant material provide nesting sites. It nests in preexisting spaces rather than excavating large galleries like some larger carpenter ants, and forages for small insects, nectar, honeydew, and other sugary resources while serving as prey for spiders, lizards, birds, and other insect-eating animals.
